reviews.title: Difficult UX
reviews.text: Some glyphs have a long press, some don’t. Larger ui’s can’t switch between tasks. Close buttons are sometimes on the top and sometimes on the bottom.  Checking things off is easy, unchecking them is difficult. Year views are not granular. I would suggest a bar chart and get rid of the connecting line or better a linear monthly calendar views like weekly dots. I think if you spend a significant amount of time with the app, it works, but coming from nothing you need to read the help to figure out how to use it since it can’t be used intuitively.

reviews.title: They should update it more. 2.5
reviews.text: I got this app a long time a go, at least 5 years ago. It was a fun and nice way of tracking progress for habits that I was trying to build. Redownloaded it and was disappointed that they hadn’t really changed it at all. I would love a way to change the end time of your day it’s annoying to retroactively go through the calendar. Would love it if I could permanently change the end of my tracked day to 2am. When you set a streak to be weekly you should be able to revise the individual days you hit or missed. For such a simple idea and the fact that I payed money for it I wish they tried more new things. More ways of motivating you, more customization, just generally more care. It’s probably a kind of important app to a lot of people and there are more ways for the developers to show that they really care for the people who are trying to build and break habits. Basically it’s a cool app but feels like it could be much cooler.

reviews.title: Good app. 1 suggestion
reviews.text:
Great app. 5 stars bc it deserves its flowers for helping people build healthy habits. 

One suggestion: make a “no more than” option for making a streak. For example, eating out, shampooing, drinks. Things that you aren’t trying to achieve but rather trying to limit to only a few times per week (or day).

reviews.title: simple, to the point, effective
reviews.text: i'm an aerospace engineering student with adhd and this app is very effective in helping me keep track of my most important habits (and things i want to quit). love how customizable it is without being overwhelming and the ability to add actions to habits (eg: i link my morning routine app). i also love that there's no subscription; it's 100% worth the $10. it also syncs very nicely between my ipad and my iphone, and i love that the ipad app is actually properly scaled to the size of the screen unlike some other apps i've tried. thank you so much!

reviews.title: Generally okay, but I wish it was easier to mark tasks as complete through the widgets.
reviews.text:
The checkmark button to click on in order to mark tasks as complete through widgets is quite small and often missed when pressed. I’ve also noticed it has a pretty delayed reaction when clicking. Also wish there was an easier/alternative way to undo task completions, more easily accessible and visible besides shaking the phone to undo (which is only available immediately after accidentally marking a task as complete).

Still overall a helpful app, and looking forward to more app updates and improvements and bug fixes over time!

reviews.title: Critical missing feature
reviews.text: This is a great app but with a critical missing feature. It lets you create streaks where you have a goal of “N per week.” This way you don’t have to do the task every day. However, you cannot see which days you completed that task. I’ll often wonder, did I already mark that task completed today? Or was it yesterday? The frustrating part is that there is even a calendar view… but it does not provide this info! Honestly without this issue I would give it 5 stars.

reviews.title: I use this app daily, and it is great, but…
reviews.text:
I’d really rather send this as suggestions to the developers because I use this app daily, and it really is helping me meet my goals.

1. For Break It Down, please remove the AI and let us add our own steps. 
2. Make an Add New Goal button, instead of having to go to the Gear button. (The Gear button = Settings. Settings ≠ New)
3. Add a Suggestion link so users don’t have to give you mediocre reviews.

reviews.title: Simple, yet powerful. Perfect for writing goals
reviews.text: I had one very specific use for this app. I am an aspiring writer and I needed a way to motivate myself to get in the habit of writing regularly. This app is PERFECT for that. I have a goal to write for 30 min 6 days a week. I love that I can set a timer right from the app. It is absolutely critical that they have a watch app too because my phone is often my source of distraction so being able to toggle things from my watch is perfect. I love that this is NOT A SUBSCRIPTION. Absolutely worth the one time cost. One of thing that is great is if you’ve been tracking with something else before this, you can retroactively add that data to the app so you don’t have to start from scratch. I’ve already written for more consecutive days using this app that I’ve managed in the last 6 months. I highly recommend.

reviews.title: So Far, So Good
reviews.text:
Since there isn’t a trial period, you have to pay to see if you like the app. $5 or $6, so what…no big deal.

I really like the interface, and how well the widgets work. Habits/Tasks are easy to set up.

My only complaint is that there isn’t a List (bar style) set up for the tasks…. So, you can see more than 6 at a time. I think that would be pretty easy to implement. It would reduce some of the friction.

Other than that. Great app.
